idiom_name: header envelope (seq id / position / size) with a dict of buffers; asyncio.Queue in-process
implementation_notes: Python's message clients expose order but not grouping: confluent-kafka's consume(num_messages) returns records in broker order, AMQP headers carry the three fields, and asyncio.Queue (or queue.Queue) already delivers FIFO within a process, which replaces the structure for in-process pipelines. Across processes the classic form is the realization: put the sequence id, position and size in the message headers, keep one buffer per sequence id, and release on the size or end marker; a gap is an error, not a wait.
pitfalls: asyncio.Queue is not thread-safe and belongs to the event loop that created it: sharing a reassembly buffer with worker threads needs queue.Queue or an explicit lock.
AMQP header values are field tables, so a position published as a string makes pos - 1 raise or silently reorder the parts.
A dict keyed by sequence id grows without bound when groups never complete; pair it with a timeout sweep (asyncio.wait_for or a janitor task).
